senses.definition: (architecture) A covered entrance to a building, whether taken from the interior, and forming a sort of vestibule within the main wall, or projecting without and with a separate roof. A porch often has chair(s), table(s) and swings.
examples: He sat on his porch, waiting for his friend to come over.

quotes.text: But Miss Thorn relieved the situation by laughing aloud,[…]. We began to tell her about Mohair and the cotillon, and of our point of observation from the Florentine galleried porch, and she insisted she would join us there.
quotes.reference: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter V, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:

senses.definition: The platform outside the external hatch of a spacecraft.

quotes.text: By the time he had put on the backpack, McDivitt was ready to let him do more—to stand on the porch at least.
